title: Size suffix with RIGHT
objective: Use RIGHT to take the size from the end of an article code, convert it to a number, and look up the pairs in stock.
instructions: Each article code in column A ends with a two-digit size. In B2:B6, extract the size with RIGHT. RIGHT returns text, so in C2:C6 turn the text size in column B into a number by multiplying it by 1. In D2:D6, look up the number in column C in the stock list in F1:G7 with XLOOKUP and show the text "No stock" when the size is not in the list. Fix the stock list with $ signs.
hints: RIGHT(text, number_of_characters) returns characters from the end of the text. =RIGHT(A2,2) gives the last two characters of A2.
RIGHT gives text, so "42" is not the number 42. Multiplying by 1 (=B2*1) turns numeric-looking text into a real number.
XLOOKUP never matches text with a number. Look up the number column C, not the text column B: =XLOOKUP(C2,$F$2:$F$7,$G$2:$G$7,"No stock").
